first: चौ॰—जौँ माे पर प्रसन्न सुखरासी। जानिय सत्य माहि निज-दासी॥
en: 'Store of joy, if you are pleased with me and truly know me as your servant, then, Lord, remove my ignorance by telling me the story of Rama in its many forms.'

first: जासु भवन सुरतरु तर होई। सह कि दरिद्र-जनित-दुख साेई॥
en: 'Can one whose house stands under the wishing tree suffer the pain of poverty? O Lord who wears the moon, think of this and remove the great confusion in my mind.'

first: प्रभु जे मुनि परमारथबादी। कहहिँ राम कहँ ब्रह्म अनादी॥
en: 'Lord, the sages who teach the highest truth call Rama the Brahman without beginning. Shesha, Sarasvati, the Vedas and the Puranas all sing the virtues of Rama.'

first: तुम्ह पुनि राम राम दिन राती। सादर जपहु अनङ्ग-अराती॥
en: 'And you, enemy of Kama, also repeat "Rama, Rama" with reverence day and night. Is this Rama the son of the king of Ayodhya, or someone else, unborn, beyond qualities and beyond knowing?'

first: दो॰—जौँ नृप-तनय त ब्रह्म किमि, नारि बिरह मति भोरि।
en: 'If he is a king's son, how can he be Brahman, when his mind was confused by grief for his wife? Seeing his deeds and hearing of his glory, my mind is badly puzzled.'

first: चौ॰—जौँ अनीह व्यापक बिभु कोऊ। कहहु बुझाइ नाथ मोहि सोऊ॥
en: 'If there is some other one, free of desire, present everywhere and all-powerful, then, Lord, explain him to me too. Knowing I am ignorant, do not be angry; do whatever will end my confusion.'

first: मैँ बन दीख राम प्रभुताई। अति-भय-विकल न तुम्हहिँ सुनाई॥
en: 'In the forest I saw Rama's greatness, but I was so troubled by fear that I did not tell you. Still my stained mind did not understand, and I fully paid the price for it.'

first: अजहूँ कछु संसय मन मोरे। करहु कृपा विनवउँ कर जोरे॥
en: 'Even now some doubt remains in my mind. I join my hands and beg you, be kind. Lord, you explained it to me in many ways then; bearing that in mind, please do not be angry.'

first: तब कर अस बिमाेह अब नाहीँ। राम-कथा पर रुचि मन माहीँ॥
en: 'I no longer have such confusion as I had then; now my heart longs for the story of Rama. Lord of the gods, who wears the king of snakes, tell me the holy tale of Rama's virtues.'

first: दो॰—बन्दउँ पद धरि धरनि सिर, विनय करउँ कर जोरि।
en: 'With my head on the ground I bow at your feet and beg you with joined hands: describe the pure glory of Rama, drawing out the essence of the Vedas.'

first: चौ॰—जदपि जोषिता अनअधिकारी। दासी मन क्रम बचन तुम्हारी॥
en: 'Though women are not thought fit for such teaching, I am your servant in mind, deed and word. The good do not hide even deep truths where they find an eager and worthy seeker.'

first: अति आरति पूछउँ सुरराया। रघुपति कथा कहहु करि दाया॥
en: 'Lord of the gods, I ask in great longing: kindly tell me the story of Rama. First think it over and tell me why Brahman, beyond all qualities, takes a form with qualities.'

first: पुनि प्रभु कहहु राम अवतारा। बालचरित पुनि कहहु उदारा॥
en: 'Then, Lord, tell me of Rama's birth, and then his noble childhood deeds. Tell how he married Janaki, and whose fault it was that he gave up the kingdom.'

first: बन बसि कीन्हे चरित अपारा। कहहु नाथ जिमि रावन मारा॥
en: 'Lord, tell me the endless deeds he did while living in the forest, and how he killed Ravana. Kind Shankar, tell me also all the many deeds he did while ruling as king.'

first: दो॰—बहुरि कहहु करुनायतन, कीन्ह जो अचरज राम।
en: 'Then, home of mercy, tell me of the wonder Rama, jewel of the Raghus, performed: how he went to his own abode together with his people.'

first: चौ॰—पुनि प्रभु कहहु सातत्व बखानी। जेहि बिज्ञान मगन मुनिज्ञानी।
en: 'Then, Lord, explain that truth in which wise sages stay absorbed. Then describe devotion, knowledge, wisdom and detachment, each one separately.'

first: अउरउ राम-रहस्य अनेका। कहहु नाथ अति बिमल बिबेका॥
en: 'Lord of pure wisdom, tell me also the many other secrets of Rama. And kind Lord, whatever I have not asked, do not keep that hidden either.'

first: तुम्ह त्रिभुवन गुरु बेद बखाना। आन जोव पाँवर का जाना।
en: 'The Vedas call you the teacher of the three worlds; what can other lowly beings know?' Uma's simple, lovely, honest questions pleased Shiva's heart.

first: हर हिय राम-चरित सब आये। प्रेम पुलक लोचन जलं छाये।
en: All Rama's deeds came into Hara's heart. His body thrilled with love and his eyes filled with tears. The form of Rama rose in his heart, and he felt the highest, boundless bliss.

first: दो॰—भगन ध्यान-रस दंड जुग, पुनि मन बाहेर कीन्ह।
en: For a short while he stayed lost in the joy of meditation; then he brought his mind back. Then Mahesha joyfully began to tell the story of Rama.

first: चौ॰—झूठउ सत्य जाहि विनु जाने। जिमि भुजङ्ग बिनु रजु पहिचाने॥
en: Without knowing him, even the false world seems true, as a rope seems a snake until it is recognised. Knowing him, the world vanishes, as the confusion of a dream goes away on waking.

first: बन्दउँ बाल-रूप सोइ रामू। सब सिधि सुलभ जपत जिसु नामू॥
en: I bow to that Rama in his child form, by repeating whose name every success comes easily. May he who is the home of good and remover of ill, who plays in Dasharatha's courtyard, show me his grace.

first: करि प्रनाम रामहिँ त्रिपुरारी। हरषि सुधा सम गिरा उचारी॥
en: After bowing to Rama, Shiva, enemy of Tripura, joyfully spoke words sweet as nectar: 'Blessed, blessed are you, daughter of the mountain king. No one does good to others as you do.'

first: पूछेहु रघुपति-कथा प्रसङ्गा। सकल-लोक जग-पावनि गङ्गा॥
en: 'You have asked about the story of Rama, which is like the Ganga that purifies all the worlds. You love Rama's feet, and you have asked these questions for the good of the world.'

first: दो॰—रामकृपा तेँ पारबति, सपनेहुँ तब मन माहिँ।
en: 'Parvati, by Rama's grace, as I see it, there is no sorrow, delusion, doubt or confusion in your mind, not even in dreams.'

first: चौ॰—तदपि असङ्का कीन्हिहु साेई। कहत सुनत सब कर हित हाई॥
en: 'Still you have raised this doubt, which is no real doubt, so that all who tell and hear the answer may gain. Those whose ears have not heard the story of Hari have ear holes like the holes of snakes.'

first: नयनन्हि सन्त दरस नहिँ देखा। लोचन माेर-पड़्ख कर लेखा॥
en: 'Eyes that have not looked on holy people are no better than the eyes on a peacock's feather. Heads that do not bow at the feet of Hari and the guru are like bitter gourds.'

first: जिन्ह हरिभगति हृदय नहिँ आनी। जीवत सव समान ते प्रानी॥
en: 'Those who have not brought devotion to Hari into their hearts are like corpses while they live. A tongue that does not sing Rama's virtues is like the tongue of a frog.'

first: कुलिस-कठोर निठुर सोइ छाती। सुनि हरि-चरित न जो हरपाती।
en: 'Hard as a thunderbolt and cruel is the heart that does not rejoice on hearing Hari's deeds. Girija, listen to the play of Rama, which helps the gods and confuses the demons.'

first: दो॰—रामकथा सुरधेनु सम, सेवत सब सुख-दानि।
en: 'The story of Rama is like the wish-granting cow; it gives every joy to those who serve it. The company of good people is like the world of the gods. Knowing this, who would not listen?'

first: चौ॰—रामकथा सुन्दर करतारी। संसय-बिहग उड़ावनिहारी॥
en: 'The story of Rama is like a sharp hand clap that frightens away the birds of doubt. It is an axe to cut down the tree of the dark age. Daughter of the mountain king, listen with respect.'

first: राम नाम गुन चरित सुहाये। जनम करम अगनित सुति गाये॥
en: 'The Vedas have sung of Rama's lovely names, virtues, deeds, births and works in countless ways. Just as Lord Rama is endless, so are his stories, glory and virtues of many kinds.'

first: तदपि जथा-सुत जसि मति माेरी। कहिहउँ देखि प्रीति अति तारी॥
en: 'Still, seeing your great love, I will tell it as I have heard it and as far as my mind allows. Uma, your questions are naturally lovely, pleasing, approved by the wise, and dear to me.'

first: एक बात नहिँ माहि सुहानी। जदपि मोह-बस कहेहु भवानी॥
en: 'But one thing did not please me, Bhavani, though you said it while confused: you said that the Rama whom the Vedas sing and on whom sages meditate is someone else.'

first: दो॰—कहहिँ सुनहिँ अस अधम नर, ग्रसे जे माह पिसाच।
en: 'Only low people, seized by the ghost of delusion, say and listen to such things: hypocrites who have turned from Hari's feet and do not know false from true.'

first: चौ॰—अज्ञ अकोबिद अन्ध अभागी। काई बिषय मुकुर-मन लागी॥
en: 'Ignorant, unlearned, blind and unlucky, the mirror of their mind is covered with the moss of worldly desire. Lustful, deceitful and very crooked, they have never seen a gathering of saints even in a dream.'

first: कहहिँ ते बेद असम्मत बानी। जिन्हहिँ न सूझ लाभ नहि हानी॥
en: 'They say things against the Vedas, for they cannot see what is gain or loss. With dirty mirrors and no eyes, how can the poor creatures see Rama's form?'

first: जिन्ह के अगुन न सगुन बिबेका। जल्पहिँ कल्पित बचन अनेका॥
en: 'They have no understanding of the formless or the form; they babble many made-up words. Lost in the world under the power of Hari's maya, there is nothing they will not say.'

first: बातुल भूत-बिबस मतवारे। ते नहिँ बोलहिँ बचन बिचारे॥
en: 'Babblers, possessed by ghosts, and drunk, they do not speak after thinking. Those who have drunk the wine of great delusion should not be listened to.'

first: सो॰—अस निज हृदय बिचारि, तजु संसय भजु राम-पद।
en: 'Think this over in your heart, give up doubt and worship Rama's feet. Listen, daughter of the mountain king: my words are rays of the sun to the darkness of confusion.'

first: चौ॰—सगुनहिँ अगुनहिँ नहिँ कछु भेदा। गावहिँ मुनि पुरान बुध वेदा॥
en: 'There is no difference between God with form and God without form; so say the sages, Puranas, the learned and the Vedas. He who is without qualities, without form, unseen and unborn, takes form out of love for his devotees.'

first: जो गुन रहित सगुन सोइ कैसे। जल-हिम-उपल बिलग नहिँ जैसे॥
en: 'How can the one without qualities be the one with qualities? Just as water, ice and hail are not different. How can one speak of delusion in him whose name is the sun to the darkness of confusion?'

first: राम सच्चिदानन्द दिनेसा। नहिँ तहँ मोह-निसा-लवलेसा॥
en: 'Rama is the sun of being, awareness and bliss; there is not the least trace of the night of delusion in him. The Lord is light by nature; for him there is not even a dawn of knowledge, for he is never in darkness.'

first: हरष बिषाद ज्ञान अज्ञाना। जीव-धरम अहमित अभिमाना॥
en: 'Joy and sorrow, knowledge and ignorance, the sense of "I" and pride, belong to living beings. The world knows Rama as Brahman, present everywhere, supreme bliss, highest Lord, the ancient one.'

first: दो॰—पुरुष-प्रसिद्ध प्रकास-निधि, प्रगट परावर-नाथ।
en: 'He who is the famous Being, the treasure of light, the Lord of all, high and low, appeared openly as the jewel of the Raghu family. He is my Lord.' Saying this, Shiva bowed his head.

first: चौ॰—निजभ्रम नहिँ समुझहिँ अज्ञानी। प्रभु परमोह धरहिँ जड़ प्रानी॥
en: 'The ignorant do not see their own mistake; the foolish put delusion on the Lord. It is like seeing a layer of clouds in the sky, and people of poor judgement say the sun is covered.'

first: चित्तव जो लोचन अङ्गुलि लाये। प्रगट जुगल ससि तेहि के भाये॥
en: 'One who presses a finger on his eye sees two moons. Uma, delusion about Rama is like that, as darkness, smoke and dust seem to be in the sky.'

first: विषय करन सुर जीव समेता। सकल एक तेँ एक सचेता॥
en: 'Sense objects, senses, the gods of the senses and the soul each are made aware by the next. The one who gives light to all of them is Rama, without beginning, the king of Ayodhya.'

first: जगत प्रकास्य प्रकासक रामू। मायाधीस ज्ञान-गुन-धामू॥
en: 'The world is what is lit, and Rama is the one who lights it: lord of maya, home of knowledge and virtue. Because of his truth, lifeless maya, helped by delusion, seems to be real.'

first: दो॰—रजत सीप महँ भास जिमि, जथा भानु-कर-वारि।
en: 'Like silver seen in a shell, or water seen in the sun's rays, though it is false at all times, no one can easily remove that illusion.'

first: चौ॰—एहि बिधि जगहरि आस्त्रित रहई। जदपि असत्य देत दुख अहई॥
en: 'In this way the world rests on Hari. Though it is unreal, it still causes pain. If someone cuts off your head in a dream, the pain does not go until you wake.'

first: जासु कृपा अस भ्रम मिटि जाई। गिरिजा सेाइ कृपालु रघुराई॥
en: 'Girija, he by whose grace such illusion is removed is the kind Lord of the Raghus. No one has found his beginning or end; the Vedas sing of him only by guessing, as far as their minds allow.'

first: बिनु पद चलइ सुनइ बिनु काना। कर बिनु करम करइ विधि नाना॥
en: 'He walks without feet and hears without ears; without hands he does many kinds of work. Without a mouth he enjoys every taste, and without a voice he is a great speaker.'

first: तन बिनु परस नयन बिनु देखा। ग्रहइ ध्रान बिनु बास असेखा।
en: 'Without a body he touches, without eyes he sees, without a nose he takes in every scent. His acts are wondrous in every way, and his glory cannot be described.'

first: दो॰—जेहि इमि गावहिँ वेद बुध, जाहि धरहिँ मुनि ध्यान।
en: 'He whom the Vedas and the wise describe like this, on whom the sages meditate, is the son of Dasharatha, the friend of devotees, the Lord, king of Kosala.'

first: चौ॰—कासी मरत जन्तु अवलोकी। जासु नाम बल करउँ बिसोकी॥
en: 'By the power of his name I free from grief the creatures I see dying in Kashi. He is my Lord, master of all moving and unmoving things, the best of the Raghus, who dwells in every heart.'

first: बिसहु जासु नाम नर कहहीँ। जनम अनेक रचित अघ दहहीँ॥
en: 'Even when people say his name helplessly, it burns away the sins of many lives. Those who remember him with reverence cross the ocean of worldly life as easily as a cow's hoofprint.'

first: राम साे परमातमा भवानी। तहँ भ्रम अति अबिहित तब बानी॥
en: 'Bhavani, that Rama is the Supreme Self. Your words of doubt about him were most unfitting. When such doubt enters the heart, knowledge, detachment and all virtues leave.'

first: सुनि सिव के सम-भञ्चन-बचना। मिटि गइ सब कुतरक कै रचना।
en: Hearing Shiva's words, which destroy confusion, all her false arguments fell apart. Love and faith for Rama's feet arose, and her terrible disbelief was gone.

first: दो॰—पुनि पुनि प्रभु-पद कमल गहि, जोरि पङ्करुह पानि।
en: Again and again she held her Lord's lotus feet, joined her lotus hands, and Girija spoke fine words that seemed soaked in love.

first: चौ॰—ससि-कर सम सुनि गिरा तुम्हारी। मिटा मोह सरदात प मारी।
en: 'Hearing your words, like moonbeams, the great heat of my delusion, like the autumn sun, has gone. Kind Lord, you have removed my doubt, and I have come to know Rama's true nature.'

first: नाथ कृपा अब गयउ विषादा। सुखी भइउँ प्रभु-चरन-प्रसादा।
en: 'Lord, by your grace my sorrow is gone; by the grace of your feet I am happy. Now look on me as your servant, though a woman is by nature dull and unknowing.'

first: प्रथम जो मैँ पूछा सोइ कहहू। जौँ मो पर प्रसन्न प्रभु अहहू॥
en: 'If you are pleased with me, Lord, tell me what I asked first. Rama is Brahman, pure awareness, undying, apart from all, and dwelling in the city of every heart.'

first: नाथ धरेउ नर तनु केहि हेतू। मीहि समुझाइ कहहु चुपकेतू॥
en: 'Lord whose banner bears the bull, explain to me why he took a human body.' Hearing Uma's very humble words, Shiva knew her love for Rama's story was pure.

first: दो॰—हिय हरषे कामारि तब, सङ्कर सहज सुजान।
en: Then Shankar, enemy of Kama and wise by nature, was glad at heart. The home of mercy praised Uma in many ways and spoke again.

first: सो॰—सुनु सुभ-कथा भवानि, रामचरितमानस बिमल।
en: 'Bhavani, listen to the blessed story, the pure Ramcharitmanas, which Bhushundi told in full and Garuda, king of birds, heard.'

first: हरि-गुन नाम अपार, कथा रूप अगनित अमित।
en: 'Hari's virtues and names have no end; his stories and forms are countless and beyond measure. I tell it as far as my mind allows; Uma, listen with respect.'

first: सो सम्बाद उदार, जेहि बिधि भा आगे कहब।
en: 'I will tell later how that noble dialogue came about. Now hear the most lovely and pure story of Rama's coming to earth.'

first: हरि गुन नाम अपार, कथा रूप अगनित अमित।
en: 'The virtues and names of Hari are without end, and the forms of his story cannot be counted or measured. As far as my understanding goes, I will tell it; Uma, hear it with reverence.'

first: चौ॰—सुनु गिरिजा हरिचरित सुहाये। बिपुल बिसद निगमागम गाये॥
en: 'Listen, Girija: the Vedas and scriptures have sung of Hari's lovely, many and pure deeds. The reason why Hari comes to earth cannot be stated as just this one thing and no other.'

first: राम अतर्क्य बुद्धि मन बानी। मत हमार अस सुनहिँ सयानी॥
en: 'Wise one, my view is this: Rama cannot be grasped by reason, mind or speech. Still, as the saints, sages, Vedas and Puranas have said something about him, each guessing by its own mind,'

first: तस मैँ सुमुखि सुनावउँ तोही। समुझि परइ जस कारन माेही॥
en: 'so, fair-faced one, I will tell you the reason as I understand it. Whenever dharma declines and wicked, proud demons grow strong,'

first: करहिँ अनीति जाइ नहिँ बरनी । सीदहिँ बिप्र-धेनु-सुर-धरनी॥
en: 'and they do wrongs beyond description, so that Brahmins, cows, gods and the earth suffer, then the Lord, ocean of mercy, takes various bodies and removes the pain of the good.'

first: दो॰—असुर मारि थापहिँ सुरन्ह, राखहिँ निज-खुति-सेतु।
en: 'He kills the demons, restores the gods, guards the limits set by his own Vedas, and spreads his pure fame in the world. These are the reasons for Rama's birth.'

first: चौ॰—साइ जस गाइ भगत भव तरहीँ। कृपासिन्धु जन-हित तनु धरहीँ।
en: 'By singing that fame devotees cross the ocean of worldly life; the ocean of mercy takes a body for the sake of his people. There are many reasons for Rama's birth, each more wonderful than the last.'

first: जनम एक दुइ कहउँ बखानी। सावधान सुनु सुमति भवानी॥
en: 'Bhavani of good mind, listen carefully; I will tell you in detail about one or two of his births. Jaya and Vijaya, as everyone knows, were the two dear doorkeepers of Hari.'

first: बिन साप तेँ दूनउँ भाई। तामस असुर देह तिन्ह पाई॥
en: 'Because of a Brahmin's curse, both brothers got the dark bodies of demons: Hiranyakashipu and Hiranyaksha, known to the world as the ones who humbled the pride of Indra.'

first: बिजई समर बीर बिख्याता। धरि बराह वपु एक निपाता॥
en: 'They were famous heroes, winners in battle. The Lord took the form of a boar and killed one of them. Then, as the man-lion, he killed the other and spread the good name of his devotee Prahlada.'

first: दो॰—भये निसाचर जाइ तेइ, महाबीर बलवान।
en: 'The same two were born again as night-roaming demons, very strong and brave: Kumbhakarna and Ravana, great warriors who conquered the gods, as the world knows.'

first: चौ॰—मुकुत न भये हते भगवाना। तीनि जनम द्विज बचन प्रमाना॥
en: 'Though killed by the Lord, they were not set free, for the Brahmin's word held for three births. Once, for their sake, the Lord who loves his devotees took a body.'

first: कस्यप अदिति तहाँ पितु माता। दसरथ कौसल्या बिख्याता॥
en: 'There, Kashyapa and Aditi became his father and mother, known as Dasharatha and Kausalya. In one age of the world he was born this way and made the world holy by his deeds.'

first: एक कलप सुर देखि दुखारे। समर जलन्धर सन सब हारे।
en: 'In another age, the gods were seen in distress, all defeated in battle by Jalandhara. Shambhu fought a mighty battle, but the very strong demon would not die however he was struck.'

first: परम-सती असुराधिप-नारी। तेहि बल ताहि न जितहिँ पुरारी ॥४॥
en: 'The demon king's wife was a most faithful woman, and by the power of her faithfulness even the enemy of Tripura could not defeat him.'

first: दो॰—छल करि टारेउ तासु ब्रत, प्रभु सुर कारज कीन्ह।
en: 'The Lord broke her vow by a trick and did the gods' work. When she learned the secret, she grew angry and cursed him.'

first: चौ॰—तासु साप हरि कीन्ह प्रबाना। कौतुक-निधि कृपाल भगवाना॥
en: 'Hari, the kind Lord who loves to play, let her curse come true. Jalandhara was born as Ravana, and Rama killed him in battle and gave him the highest state.'

first: एक जनम कर कारन एहा। जेहि लगि राम धरी नर-देहा॥
en: 'This was the reason for one birth in which Rama took a human body. Listen, sage: poets have told at length the story of each of the Lord's comings.'

first: नारद साप दीन्ह एक बारा। कलप एक तेहि लगि अवतारा॥
en: 'Once Narada gave a curse, and for that the Lord came down in one age.' Girija was amazed to hear this: 'But Narada is a devotee of Vishnu, and wise!'

first: कारन कवन साप मुनि दीन्हा। का अपराध रमापति कीन्हा।
en: 'For what reason did the sage curse him? What wrong had Lakshmi's lord done? Tell me this story, enemy of Tripura. Delusion in the sage's mind is a great wonder.'

first: दो॰—बोले बिहँसि महेस तब, ज्ञानी मूढ़ न कोइ।
en: Then Mahesha smiled and said, 'No one is wise or foolish by himself. Whatever Rama makes a person at any moment, that he becomes at once.'

first: सो॰—कहउँ राम-गुन गाथ, भरद्वाज सादर सुनहु।
en: 'I tell the tale of Rama's virtues; Bharadvaja, listen with respect.' Tulsi says: Rama destroys the fear of worldly life; give up pride and arrogance and worship him.

first: चौ॰—हिम गिरि गुहा एक अति पावनि। बह समीप सुरसरी सुहावनि॥
en: In the Himalaya there was a very holy cave, near which the lovely heavenly river flowed. Seeing the most pure and beautiful hermitage, the divine sage Narada was delighted.

first: निरखि सैल सरि बिपिन विभागा। भयउ रमापति-पद अनुरागा॥
en: Seeing the mountains, river and forest all around, love for the feet of Lakshmi's lord rose in him. As he remembered Hari, the force of a curse on him was stopped, and his naturally pure mind went into deep meditation.

first: मुनि गति देखि सुरेस डराना। कामहिँ बोलि कीन्ह सनमाना॥
en: Seeing the sage's state, Indra grew afraid. He called Kama, honoured him and said, 'Go with your helpers for my sake.' The fish-bannered god set out with a glad heart.

first: सुनासीर मन महँ असि त्रासा। चहत देवरिषि मम पुर बासा।
en: Indra feared in his mind that the divine sage wanted to take his city. Those in the world who are lustful and greedy fear everyone, like the crooked crow.

first: दो॰—सूख हाड़ लेइ भाग सठ, स्वान निरखि मृगराज।
en: Like a foolish dog that runs off with a dry bone when it sees a lion, thinking the lion may snatch it away, so Indra felt no shame.

first: चौ॰—तेहि आस्त्रमहि मदन जब गयऊ। निज माया बसन्त निरमयऊ।
en: When Kama went to that hermitage, he created spring by his magic. Trees of many kinds bloomed in many colours, cuckoos called and bees hummed.

first: चली सुहावनि त्रिबिध बयारी। काम-कृसानु बढ़ावनि हारी।
en: A pleasant breeze blew, cool, gentle and fragrant, feeding the fire of desire. Rambha and other young heavenly women, all skilled in the arts of love,

first: करहिँ गान बहु तान तरङ्गा। बहु बिधि क्रीड़हिँ पानि-पतङ्गा॥
en: sang in many rising tunes and made many playful gestures with their hands. Seeing his helpers, Kama was pleased and then tried many kinds of tricks.

first: काम-कला कछु मुनिहिँ न ब्यापी। निज-भय डरेउ मनेाभव पापो॥
en: But Kama's arts had no effect on the sage, and the wicked god of love became afraid of his own fate. Can anyone break the bounds of one whose great protector is Lakshmi's lord?

first: दो॰—सहित सहाय समीत अति, मानि हारि मन मैन।
en: Kama and his helpers were very afraid. Admitting defeat in his heart, he went and held the sage's feet and spoke very humble words.

first: चौ॰—भयउ न नारद मन कछु रोषा। कहि प्रिय बचन काम परितोषा।
en: Narada felt no anger at all. He comforted Kama with kind words. Kama bowed at his feet, took his leave and went away with his helpers.

first: मुनि सुसीलता आपनि करनी। सुरपति-सभा जाइ सब बरनी॥
en: He went to Indra's court and told them about the sage's goodness and his own deeds. Everyone was amazed to hear it; they praised the sage and bowed to Hari.

first: तव नारद गवने सिव पाहीँ। जिता काम अहमिति मन माहीँ।
en: Then Narada went to Shiva, with pride in his heart at having conquered Kama. He told Shankar the story of Kama, and Mahesha, knowing him very dear, gave him advice.

first: बार बार बिनवउँ मुनि तोही। जिमि यह कथा सुनायहु माेही॥
en: 'Sage, I beg you again and again: do not ever tell this story to Hari the way you have told it to me. Even if the subject comes up, keep it hidden.'

first: दो॰—सम्भु दीन्ह उपदेस हित, नहिँ नारदहि सोहान।
en: Shambhu gave this advice for his good, but Narada did not like it. Bharadvaja, hear this curious tale: Hari's will is strong.

first: चौ॰—राम कीन्ह चाहहिँ साेइ होई। करइ अन्यथा अस नहिँ कोई॥
en: Whatever Rama wishes to do, that happens; no one can make it otherwise. The sage did not like Shiva's words, and he went to Brahma's world.

first: एक बार करतल बर-बीना। गावत हरि-गुन गान-प्रबीना॥
en: Once the great sage, skilled in song, with a fine vina in his hand, went singing Hari's praises to the ocean of milk, where Lakshmi's lord, the crown of the Vedas, lives.

first: हरषि मिले उठि रमानिकेता। बैठे आसन रिषिहि समेता॥
en: Lakshmi's lord rose joyfully to meet him and sat down with the sage. The Lord of all moving and unmoving things smiled and said, 'Sage, you have shown kindness after many days.'

first: काम-चरित नारद सब भाखे। जद्यपि प्रथम बरजि सिव राखे॥
en: Narada told him the whole story of Kama, though Shiva had warned him against it before. Rama's maya is very powerful; who in the world has been born whom it does not deceive?

first: दो॰—रूख बदन करि बचन मृदु, बोले श्रीभगवान।
en: The Lord made a grave face and spoke gentle words: 'By remembering you, delusion, lust, pride and vanity disappear.'

first: चौ॰—सुनु मुनि मोह हाेइ मन ताके। ज्ञान बिराग हृदय नहिं जाके॥
en: 'Listen, sage: delusion arises in the mind of one who has no knowledge or detachment in his heart. You keep the vow of celibacy and are very steady of mind; can Kama trouble you?'

first: नारद कहेउ सहित अभिमाना। कृपा तुम्हारि सकल भगवाना॥
en: Narada said with pride, 'Lord, it is all your grace.' The ocean of mercy thought it over and saw that a great tree of pride had sprouted in his heart.

first: बेगि सो मैं डारिहउँ उपारी। पन हमार सेवक-हितकारी॥
en: 'I will quickly pull it up by the roots, for it is my vow to do good to my servants. I will surely find a way that will be for the sage's good and a game for me.'

first: तब नारद हरि-पद सिर नाई। चले हृदय अहमिति अधिकाई॥
en: Then Narada bowed his head at Hari's feet and left, with even more pride in his heart. Then Lakshmi's lord set his own maya to work. Now hear what harsh things it did.

first: दो॰—विरचेल भग महँ नगर तेहि, सत जोजन विस्तार।
en: On the road it made a city a hundred yojanas wide, built in many ways finer than the city of Vishnu himself.

first: चौ॰—बसहिँ नगर सुन्दर नर नारी। जनु बहु मनसिज-रति तनु धारी॥
en: Beautiful men and women lived in the city, as if many Kamas and Ratis had taken bodies. In that city lived King Shilanidhi, with countless horses, elephants, soldiers and people.

first: सत-सुरेस सम बिभव बिलासा। रूप तेज बल नीति निवासा॥
en: His wealth and pleasures equalled those of a hundred Indras; he was the home of beauty, glory, strength and good rule. His daughter was Vishvamohini, whose beauty charmed even Lakshmi.

first: सोइ हरि माया सब गुन खानी। सोभा तासु कि जाइ बखानी॥
en: She was Hari's maya itself, a mine of every virtue; can her beauty be described? The princess was holding a ceremony to choose her husband, and countless kings had come there.

first: मुनि कौतुकी नगर तेहि गयऊ। पुरबासिन्ह सब पूछत भयऊ॥
en: The curious sage went to that city and asked the people there about everything. Hearing all of it, he came to the palace, and the king honoured the sage and gave him a seat.

first: दो॰—आनि देखाई नारदहि, भूपति राजकुमारि।
en: The king brought the princess and showed her to Narada, saying, 'Lord, think it over and tell me all her good and bad points.'

first: चौ॰—देखि रूप मुनि बिरति बिसारी। बड़ी बार लगि रहे निहारी॥
en: Seeing her beauty, the sage forgot his detachment and kept gazing at her for a long time. Looking at the signs on her body, he lost himself. He rejoiced in his heart but did not say so openly.

first: जो एहि बरइ अमर सोइ होई। समर भूमि तेहि जीत न कोई॥
en: 'Whoever marries her will become immortal, and no one will defeat him in battle. All moving and unmoving beings will serve the man whom Shilanidhi's daughter chooses.'

first: लच्छन सब बिचारि उर राखे। कछुक धनाइ भूप सल भाखे॥
en: He kept all these signs to himself after thinking them over, and told the king something made up. Saying to the king, 'Your daughter has fine signs,' Narada left, with worry in his mind.

first: करउँ जाइ सोइ जतन बिचारी। जेहि प्रकार माेहि बरइ कुमारी॥
en: 'I must go and think of some way to make this girl choose me. There is no time now for prayer or penance. O Creator, how can I win this girl?'

first: दो॰—एहि अवसर चाहिय परम, सोभा रूप बिसाल।
en: 'At this time I need the greatest beauty and a splendid form, so that the princess is charmed when she sees me and puts the victory garland on me.'

first: चौ॰—हरि सन माँगउँ सुन्दरताई। होइहि जात गहरु मोहि भाई॥
en: 'I will ask Hari for beauty, but brother, going there will take too long. No one wishes me well like Hari; may he help me at this time.'

first: बहु बिधि बिनय कीन्ह तेहि काला। प्रगटेउ प्रभु कौतुकी कृपाला॥
en: Then he prayed in many ways, and the kind, playful Lord appeared. Seeing the Lord, the sage's eyes were soothed, and he rejoiced, thinking the work would now be done.

first: अति आरति कहि कथा सुनाई। करहु कृपा करि होहु सहाई॥
en: In great distress he told the whole story: 'Be kind and help me. Lord, give me your own form; there is no other way I can win her.'

first: जेहि बिधि नाथ होइ हित माेरा। करहु से बेगि दास मैँ ताेरा॥
en: 'Lord, do quickly whatever will be good for me; I am your servant.' Seeing the great power of his own maya, the Lord who is kind to the humble laughed inwardly and spoke.

first: दो॰—जेहि बिधि होइहि परम हित, नारद सुनहु तुम्हार।
en: 'Listen, Narada: I will do whatever will be for your highest good, and nothing else. My word is never false.'

first: चौ॰—कुपथ माँग रुज व्याकुल रोगी। बैद न देइ सुनहु मुनि जोगी॥
en: 'Listen, sage and yogi: when a sick man in pain asks for harmful food, the doctor does not give it. In the same way I have set my mind on your good.' Saying this, the Lord vanished.

first: माया बिबस भये मुनि मूढ़ा। समुझी नहिँ हरि गिरा निगूढ़ा॥
en: Under the spell of maya the sage became so foolish that he did not understand Hari's deep words. The great sage went at once to where the ground for the bride's choice had been made ready.

first: निज निज आसन बैठे राजा। बहु बनाव करि सहित समाजा॥
en: The kings, finely dressed, sat in their seats with their followers. The sage was glad in his heart: 'My form is so handsome; she will never by mistake choose anyone but me.'

first: मुनि हित कारन कृपानिधाना। दीन्ह कुरूप न जाइ बखाना॥
en: For the sage's good, the ocean of mercy had given him an ugly form beyond description. No one could see this trick; thinking him Narada, everyone bowed to him.

first: दो॰—रहे तहाँ दुइ रुद्र गन, ते जानहिँ सब भेउ।
en: Two of Rudra's attendants were there who knew the whole secret. Dressed as Brahmins, they went about watching; they too loved a good joke.
